title: Concurrent Write Grading V1
description: How the database grades a write it commits against the other authors' writes: only a write committed after the operation the author `observed` (advisory authoring context, never an ordering constraint) and by another actor is concurrent with it; a concurrent write conflicts when both touch the same fields (the database reads a path-map diff) or, for diffs opaque to it, when their declared targets overlap (an empty target is the whole artifact). A conflict is `mutation.clamped` (Warning): `normal` accepts the write with the message, `vigilant` refuses it. A supersession (history editing) writes fields: it is graded and conflicts like a write by the target its replacement operations declare (a withdrawal declares the withdrawn operation's target); it may name any author's operation, but only one the log holds (`history.unknown-target`, refused whatever the policy). Every other history transition is never graded and never conflicts.

observed.description: The newest operation of another author the author had applied.

oneOf.description: An opaque (plugin) diff and the target its mutation declares.
A path-map diff the database reads.
A supersession: a history transition that replaces the effective input of committed operations.

target.description: The superseded operation; the envelope depends on exactly these.

replacement.description: A replacement input, or a withdrawal that folds the operation as a no-op.

target.description: The declared target: the replacement operations' conflict targets, the withdrawn operations' own for a withdrawal.

codes.description: Every message code the submit reports, in order.
